newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian edible oil eases on good import arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian edible oil eases on good import arrivals.

text.p: Indian edible oil prices eased by about 200 rupees ($5.6) to 800 rupees per tonne during the past week due to good arrivals of sunflower oil from Argentina and the United States, industry officials and traders said on Wednesday.
"Prices have become soft because of arrivals of imported edible oil," Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange, told Reuters.
Shah said about 50,000 tonnes of sunflower oil had reached Indian ports.

Industry officials had earlier said India had signed contracts to import around 150,000 tonnes of sunflower for shipments between January and March compared with 60,000 tonnes of palm olein for the same period.
They said sunflower imports during 1996/97 (November-October) are expected to surge to around 250,000 tonnes as prices of Malaysian palm olein had shot up during the past month.
Indian imported 110,000 tonnes of sunflower oil in 1995/96.
"Around 5,000 tonnes of palm olein oil are also arriving from Malaysia every week," Shah said.
Traders said groundnut oil was currently quoted at around 34,000 rupees per tonne compared with 34,300 rupees last week. Palm olein was quoted at around 28,000 rupees against 28,200 rupees last week.
Sunflower (crude) was quoted at around 27,000 rupees against 27,800 rupees last week, traders said.
Industry officials and traders said the winter oilseed crop is expected be lower than earlier estimated.
"The output will be at least five percent lower from what was earlier anticipated," Shah said.
The Agriculture Ministry has estimated the 1996/97 winter oilseed crop at around 12.7 million compared to 12.01 million last year. It has predicted the summer crop at around 9.5 million.
But trade estimates project this year's winter crop at 11.91 million tonnes, only marginally up from 11.43 million last year.
India harvests two oilseed crops annually, with the bulk of its output from the winter crop. The winter crop is sown in July and harvested from October.
-- Sambit Mohanty New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024 ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
